title: Color Grading LUT Editor with Histogram
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements an interactive Color Grading LUT (Look-Up Table) editor with a real-time histogram display.

## Scene Setup
- Use a Three.js WebGLRenderer with a canvas filling the left 65% of the viewport.
- Load or procedurally generate a textured 3D scene to preview color grading on: place a rotating cube (size 2) with a procedural checkerboard texture, a sphere (radius 1) with a gradient texture, and a torus knot with a colorful procedural texture. Position them in a row along the X axis at (-3, 0, 0), (0, 0, 0), and (3, 0, 0).
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 3, 10) looking at origin.
- Add an AmbientLight (intensity 0.4) and a DirectionalLight at (5, 10, 7) with intensity 0.8.
- The scene must be rendered to an offscreen RenderTarget first, then a fullscreen quad applies the LUT color grading as a post-process using a custom ShaderMaterial before displaying to screen.

## LUT System
- Implement a 1D LUT with 3 independent channel curves: Red, Green, Blue.
- Each channel curve is defined by 5 control points along the 0-1 input range at positions [0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0]. Each control point has an output value (initially equal to input, i.e., identity mapping: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0).
- Interpolate between control points using linear interpolation to build a 256-entry LUT texture (a DataTexture of size 256x1 with RGB channels).
- The post-process shader samples this LUT texture to remap each pixel's R, G, B channels independently.

## UI Panel (right 35% of viewport)
- Create a DOM-based panel with id='lut-panel' on the right side with a dark background (#1a1a2e).
- At the top, display a histogram canvas (id='histogram-canvas', 300x150 pixels) that shows the RGB histogram of the final graded image. Draw R, G, B histograms as semi-transparent overlapping filled curves (R: rgba(255,0,0,0.5), G: rgba(0,255,0,0.5), B: rgba(0,0,255,0.5)).
- Below the histogram, show the LUT curve editor: a canvas (id='curve-canvas', 300x200 pixels) with a dark grid background. Draw the three channel curves (R, G, B) as colored lines. The identity (diagonal) line should be drawn as a dashed gray line for reference.
- Below the curve editor, add channel selector buttons: 'Red' (id='btn-red'), 'Green' (id='btn-green'), 'Blue' (id='btn-blue'), 'All' (id='btn-all'). The active channel button should have a highlighted border. Default active channel is 'All'.
- Add a 'Reset' button (id='btn-reset') that resets all curves to identity.
- Add a 'Brightness' slider (id='slider-brightness', range -100 to 100, default 0) and a 'Contrast' slider (id='slider-contrast', range -100 to 100, default 0). These apply a global brightness/contrast adjustment BEFORE the LUT is applied.
- Add a label (id='label-avg-luminance') that displays the average luminance of the graded image, updated each frame.

## Interactions
- Clicking on the curve canvas selects the nearest control point of the active channel(s) and allows dragging it vertically to change its output value (clamped to 0-1). The X position of control points is fixed.
- When 'All' is selected, dragging affects all three channels simultaneously.
- The histogram and average luminance must update in real-time as curves or sliders change.
- Keyboard: Press 'I' to toggle invert mode (flips all curves: output = 1 - output for each control point). Press 'S' to toggle a sepia preset (set R curve outputs to [0, 0.3, 0.55, 0.78, 0.95], G curve to [0, 0.22, 0.45, 0.68, 0.85], B curve to [0, 0.15, 0.35, 0.55, 0.7]). Press 'D' to reset to identity (same as Reset button).

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- lutR: array of 5 output values for Red channel control points
- lutG: array of 5 output values for Green channel control points
- lutB: array of 5 output values for Blue channel control points
- activeChannel: string 'red'|'green'|'blue'|'all'
- brightness: number (-100 to 100)
- contrast: number (-100 to 100)
- invertMode: boolean
- avgLuminance: number (0-1 range, computed from graded image)
- histogramR: array of 256 integers (bin counts for red channel)
- histogramG: array of 256 integers (bin counts for green channel)
- histogramB: array of 256 integers (bin counts for blue channel)
- histogramMaxBin: number (the maximum bin count across all channels, used for normalization)
- frameCount: number incremented each render frame
- objectsLoaded: boolean (true once all 3 meshes are created)
- lutTextureSize: number (should be 256)
- postProcessActive: boolean (true when post-process shader is active)

## Technical Requirements
- The LUT DataTexture must be updated every frame (or when curves change).
- Read back pixels from the rendered framebuffer (using renderer.readRenderTargetPixels) to compute the histogram and average luminance.
- Objects should slowly rotate (cube around Y, sphere around X, torus knot around Z) for visual variety.
- Ensure all numerical state values are never NaN or undefined.
physics_constraints: LUT output values must be clamped to [0, 1]. Brightness and contrast must be clamped to [-100, 100]. Histogram bin counts must be non-negative integers. Average luminance must be in [0, 1]. Control point X positions are fixed at [0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0]. Linear interpolation between control points must produce monotonic-safe but not necessarily monotonic curves (output values can be any value in [0,1]).
